carrots-canned-reduced-sodium-cooked-no-.title: Carrots, canned, reduced sodium, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Reduced‑sodium canned carrots are a ready‑to‑eat vegetable that has been cooked, had excess salt removed, and contains no added fat. The product is shelf‑stable and convenient for cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Carrots are one of the most widely consumed root vegetables worldwide.
Reduced sodium is achieved by replacing part of the salt with milder flavor enhancers.
Quick heat processing helps retain most of the beta‑carotene (vitamin A precursor).
No added fat makes the product low‑calorie, suitable for diet plans.
A sealed can can keep carrots fresh for 2‑3 years at room temperature.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene converts to vitamin A in the body, supporting vision and immune function.

items.title: Low sodium content
items.content: Reduced salt helps maintain healthy blood pressure.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Carrots contain antioxidants that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Heart‑healthy
items.content: The combination of fiber, potassium, and low sodium benefits cardiovascular health.

items.title: Carrot allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to carrots.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Certain canned varieties may contain a small amount of added sugar.

items.title: Can material
items.content: Long‑term storage in metal cans can sometimes cause slight flavor changes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add canned carrots to salads, soups, stews, use as a side dish, or enjoy as a snack. They can be diced or sliced for easy incorporation.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened can in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the carrots in a sealed container in the refrigerator and consume within 5‑7 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Fruit juice, acai blend (5530) is a ready‑to‑drink beverage made from selected acai berries, apples, oranges and mangoes. It offers a bright berry flavor, a rich aroma and the characteristic deep purple hue of acai.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Acai berries grow in the tropical Amazon region and are renowned for their high antioxidant content.
The juice combines several fruits, enhancing both taste complexity and nutritional value.
Natural acidity of the fruits eliminates the need for artificial preservatives.
In the 2020s, acai‑based drinks saw a rapid rise in popularity across Europe and North America.
Packaging in dark glass bottles helps preserve light‑sensitive nutrients.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Acai berries contain anthocyanins and polyphenols that help neutralize free radicals and support cellular health.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C from oranges and mangoes boosts the body's immune defenses.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Acai provides plant‑based omega‑3 and omega‑6 fatty acids, beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: Fiber from apples and mangoes promotes regular bowel movements and a feeling of fullness.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The juice supplies vitamins B1, B2 and B6, essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Fruit allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to citrus or berries may experience a reaction to this product.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although no sugar is added, the natural fruit sugars (fructose) may affect blood glucose levels; diabetics should monitor portion size.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity can irritate the stomach lining in sensitive persons.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The juice is ready to drink straight from the bottle. It can be enjoyed chilled, used in smoothies, cocktails, or as a base for fruit desserts. For a milder taste, dilute with water.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bottle in the refrigerator at 2 °C–6 °C. Once opened, consume within 5–7 days. Keep away from direct sunlight.

content.title: About
content.content: Raw mushrooms are edible fruiting bodies of various fungi, harvested from the wild or cultivated on farms. They have a delicate, slightly earthy flavor and a tender, sometimes crisp texture. Raw mushrooms are used in salads, marinades, dried as snacks, or as an ingredient in dishes that are not cooked.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mushrooms belong to a separate kingdom of organisms, distinct from plants and animals.
There are over 10,000 edible mushroom species, but only a small fraction are widely available in stores.
Mushrooms can synthesize vitamin D2 when exposed to ultraviolet light.
Some varieties, such as button mushrooms, can be farm‑grown year‑round under controlled conditions.
Mushroom mycelium plays a key role in decomposing organic matter and maintaining soil health.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Raw mushrooms provide niacin, riboflavin, thiamine, and folate, which support energy metabolism and the nervous system.

items.title: Low‑calorie protein source
items.content: Mushrooms deliver plant protein with few calories, making them useful for weight management.

items.title: Source of selenium
items.content: Selenium in mushrooms has antioxidant properties and supports immune function.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: High in polyphenols
items.content: Antioxidant polyphenols help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Poisoning risk
items.content: Foraging wild mushrooms without proper identification can lead to consumption of toxic species.

items.title: Digestive difficulty
items.content: Some people may experience gas or stomach discomfort from raw mushrooms.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Although rare, allergies to certain mushroom varieties can occur.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Mushrooms are high in purines, which may be a concern for individuals with gout.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw mushrooms can be thinly sliced and added to salads, pickled in vinegar, used in ceviche or sushi rolls. Before eating, they should be thoroughly rinsed and, if desired, marinated to reduce any microbial risk.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store raw mushrooms in a paper bag or a container with ventilation in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. They keep for 3‑5 days. Avoid airtight plastic bags, which accelerate spoilage.

pasta-with-cream-sauce-and-poultry-ready.title: Pasta with Cream Sauce and Poultry, Ready‑to‑Heat

content.title: About
content.content: Pasta with cream sauce and pieces of chicken meat is a ready‑to‑heat meal designed for quick warming in a microwave or on the stove. It contains durum wheat pasta, a smooth cream sauce, and selected chicken breast, seasoned with herbs and spices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish is engineered for convenience: only 3‑5 minutes of heating are required.
The cream sauce is made from dairy and vegetable oils, giving a velvety texture without excess fat.
Chicken used is lean breast meat, a high‑quality source of protein.
Durum wheat pasta retains its shape even after long shelf life.
The product undergoes thermal processing to ensure microbiological safety.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Chicken provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair and maintenance.

items.title: Energy supply
items.content: Carbohydrates from the pasta deliver a quick source of energy, convenient for busy schedules.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: The cream sauce contains dairy ingredients that are sources of calcium and vitamin D for bone health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both pasta and chicken are rich in B1, B2, B3 vitamins, supporting metabolic processes.

items.title: Low trans‑fat content
items.content: Vegetable oils used in the recipe are free of trans fats, making the product more heart‑friendly.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: The cream sauce may trigger reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: People monitoring salt intake should consider the product’s sodium level.

items.title: Heat treatment
items.content: Follow the recommended heating times to avoid overheating and loss of flavor.

items.title: Post‑opening storage
items.content: After opening, keep the product refrigerated and consume within 2‑3 days.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Remove the pouch from the outer pack, transfer the contents to a microwave‑safe dish or saucepan, add 100‑150 ml of water, cover, and heat for 3‑5 minutes in the microwave (or 5‑7 minutes on the stove, stirring). Mix well before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a dry, cool place at temperatures between 0 °C and +25 °C. Shelf life is indicated on the package. After opening, keep refrigerated.

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken cream soup is a thick, velvety puree‑style soup made from chicken fillet, broth, cream, and aromatic spices. It has a mild buttery flavor with a subtle chicken note and a silky texture, perfect as a starter on a cold day.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken cream soup emerged in the early 20th century as a haute‑cuisine dish in Europe.
Traditionally it is prepared from chicken broth, cream, and pureed cooked vegetables such as potato, carrot, and onion.
In Russia its popularity rose after canned versions appeared in the 1950s.
The soup is often served with croutons, fresh herbs, or grated cheese.
Many variations exist: with mushrooms, corn, spinach, or ginger.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: The soup supplies niacin, vitamin B6 and riboflavin, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Chicken and vegetables deliver iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for immunity and bone health.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The pureed texture and gentle cooking make the soup easy on the stomach, beneficial during colds.

items.title: Hydration support
items.content: The broth provides fluids and electrolytes, helping maintain proper hydration.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to chicken or eggs and should avoid the product.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Cream adds calories and saturated fat, so portion size should be monitored.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Prepared cream soups often contain added salt; people with hypertension should choose low‑sodium versions.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Improper storage can allow bacterial growth, so cool the soup quickly and keep it refrigerated.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the soup hot, bringing it to a gentle boil. Garnish with croutons, fresh herbs, grated Parmesan, or a drizzle of olive oil. For a lighter version, replace cream with low‑fat yogurt or milk.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the finished cream soup in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3‑4 days. For longer keeping, freeze it in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months. Reheat to a boil before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Tabbouleh is a traditional Middle Eastern salad made from bulgur (or couscous), fresh vegetables, herbs, lemon juice, and olive oil. It has a light, refreshing texture and a characteristic tangy‑sweet flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name comes from the Arabic word “tabboul,” meaning “seasoning.”
Classic recipes use bulgur, but some regions substitute couscous or even quinoa.
Tabbouleh is often served as a mezze dish alongside hummus, falafel, and pita.
It is believed to have originated in Lebanon in the 19th century and spread throughout the Mediterranean.
Lemon juice not only adds flavor but also helps keep the vegetables bright.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Bulghur and vegetables provide both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Low‑calorie
items.content: Tabbouleh is low in calories, making it a good choice for weight management.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Lemon juice and fresh veggies supply vitamin C, which supports the immune system.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes, parsley, and mint are rich in antioxidants that combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Olive oil adds monounsaturated fats that are beneficial for cardiovascular health.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Bulghur contains gluten, so people with celiac disease should use gluten‑free alternatives.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: A large amount of lemon juice may irritate the stomach in individuals with high acidity.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Over‑salting can be an issue for those monitoring sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve tabbouleh chilled as an appetizer or side dish with grilled meats, fish, or kebabs. It can be added to sandwiches, used as a filling for vegetable wraps, or simply eaten with a spoon.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep tabbouleh in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, keep the dressing and vegetables separate to maintain crunchiness.

content.title: About
content.content: Yogurt is a fermented dairy food made by adding live bacterial cultures to milk. The bacteria convert milk sugar into lactic acid, which thickens the milk and gives yogurt its tangy flavor. Yogurt comes in many styles, including plain, Greek, drinkable, and flavored, and is eaten on its own, in smoothies, sauces, and desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Yogurt is traditionally made with the bacteria Lactobacillus bulgaricus and Streptococcus thermophilus.
Greek yogurt is strained to remove whey, making it thicker and higher in protein.
Yogurt-like fermented milks have been made for thousands of years in Central Asia, the Middle East, and the Balkans.
A "live and active cultures" label shows that live bacteria are present in the product.
Fermentation lowers the lactose content compared with milk.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Yogurt provides protein that supports muscle maintenance and fullness, especially Greek yogurt.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Yogurt is a good source of calcium, which supports bones and teeth.

items.title: Provides B vitamins
items.content: Yogurt contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin (B2).

items.title: Contains live cultures
items.content: Yogurt with live cultures may support digestive health.

items.title: May be easier to digest than milk
items.content: The bacteria in yogurt break down some lactose, which many people with mild lactose intolerance find easier to tolerate.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: Yogurt contains milk protein and should be avoided by people allergic to milk.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Yogurt still contains some lactose and may cause discomfort in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Added sugar
items.content: Flavored and sweetened yogurts can contain a lot of added sugar, so check labels.

items.title: Medication interactions and weakened immunity
items.content: Calcium in dairy can reduce the absorption of some medications, such as certain antibiotics. People with weakened immunity should ask a healthcare professional about live-culture products.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Yogurt can be eaten plain or with fruit, nuts, honey, or granola, blended into smoothies, or used in dressings, marinades, sauces, and baking. Plain yogurt is a good base for adding your own flavorings. It can replace sour cream or mayonnaise in some recipes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep yogurt refrigerated and use it by the date on the package. After opening, close the container tightly, use a clean spoon, and eat it within about a week. A little liquid on top is normal whey and can be stirred in. Discard yogurt that smells off or has mold.
